question_text: The stomatal pore is guarded by two kidney shaped guard cells. Name the epidermal cells surrounding the guard cells. How does a guard cell differ from an epidermal cell? Use a diagram to illustrate your answer.

page_header: Histology and Anatomy of Flowering Plants · 4 marks

steps.label: The surrounding cells
steps.margin_note: Two lines. Give both accepted names.
lines: The stomatal pore is bounded by two kidney
shaped, that is bean shaped, guard cells.
The epidermal cells that surround these guard
cells are called subsidiary cells or accessory
cells.
steps.why: The question names the guard cells for you and asks only for the cells around them, so this mark is a single term. Subsidiary and accessory are the two accepted words.
common_mistakes: Writing complementary cells. Those belong to a lenticel, not to a stoma.
Answering epidermal cells only. The marked term is subsidiary or accessory cells.
steps.memory_tip: Subsidiary means helping, so these are the cells that assist the guard cells.

steps.label: How a guard cell differs
steps.margin_note: Two marks here. Number the differences so the examiner can count them.
lines: A guard cell differs from an ordinary
epidermal cell in the following characters:
1. It is smaller in size.
2. It is bean shaped in dicots and dumb-bell
shaped in monocots, while an epidermal cell
has no such fixed shape.
3. Its wall is unevenly thickened. In a bean
shaped guard cell the outer wall is thin and
the inner wall is thick. In a dumb-bell shaped
guard cell the middle wall is thick and the
end walls are thin.
4. It contains chloroplasts. The other
epidermal cells have none.
5. It opens and closes the pore, so it
controls transpiration and the exchange of
gases.
steps.why: Uneven wall thickening is the point the other differences hang on: because one wall is thicker than the other, the cell bends when it takes up water, and that bending is what opens the pore.
common_mistakes: Saying every epidermal cell has chloroplasts. Only the guard cells do.
Reversing the thick wall. In a bean shaped guard cell the inner wall is the thick one.
Giving the shapes and stopping. The function is also marked.
steps.memory_tip: Small, shaped, unevenly thickened, green, and able to close: five differences in that order.

steps.label: Diagram of a stoma
steps.margin_note: Label epidermal cell, subsidiary cells, guard cells, chloroplast and stomatal pore.
steps.why: The question asks for a diagram in so many words, so a drawing is a separate mark. The picture also proves the shapes and the position of the chloroplasts without any extra sentence.
common_mistakes: Drawing the pore between the subsidiary cells. The pore lies between the two guard cells.
Putting chloroplast dots in the epidermal cells as well.
steps.memory_tip: Two beans facing each other, a gap between them, and dots inside the beans only.

insider_note: The words 'use a diagram' in the question make the drawing compulsory. An answer with all five differences and no diagram still loses a mark.
